purpose: Hard acceptance gate for claiming that untouched JAM 4.6 runs through the native OpenMW xNVSE compatibility stack with retail-parity behavior.
claimAllowedOnlyWhenPassed: Untouched JAM 4.6 executes all nine shipped gameplay modules through xNVSE-compatible command and event dispatch backed by real OpenMW systems.

runtimeGates.coverageRule: Every active provider command reached by the scenarios must have a successful dispatch and native-effect telemetry record. Every active command in the static JAM footprint must be implemented or explicitly proven unreachable under the recorded JAM configuration; returning zero from an unknown-command fallback is always a failure.

capturePolicy.overlayRule: The overlay must be rendered from the same timestamped telemetry records consumed by the proof validator. Static or hand-authored plugin-loaded labels do not count.
capturePolicy.comparisonRule: Retail FNV and OpenMW must run the same save, configuration, input sequence, camera heading, route, target IDs, and scenario order. Each side remains visible throughout its scenario interval.

layers.label: xNVSE core
layers.requiredAttestation: Expression evaluation, arrays, strings, UDF invocation, event registration/dispatch, command dispatch, and save/reload serialization each produce a successful telemetry-backed state change.

layers.label: JIP LN
layers.requiredAttestation: Every JIP LN command used by a recorded JAM branch dispatches to a named native OpenMW engine path and produces its expected effect.

layers.label: JohnnyGuitar
layers.requiredAttestation: Every JohnnyGuitar callback or command used by a recorded JAM branch is raised by the corresponding native OpenMW event source and reaches the registered UDF.

layers.label: kNVSE
layers.requiredAttestation: Because JAM 4.6 has zero active direct kNVSE calls, a separately labelled provider probe must install, play, observe, and restore a real animation override through the native OpenMW animation controller. It must not be represented as a JAM command.

scenarios.title: Just Dynamic Crosshair
scenarios.trigger: Equip the matched firearm, hold the camera on the fixture target, stand still, walk, run, fire, recover, aim down sights, sweep across an interactable, and sweep across a hostile actor.
assertions: JAM's JDC XML and DDS assets render instead of a proof-drawn reticle.
The measured reticle extent increases with the computed spread and contracts after movement or firing stops.
The original vanilla reticle visibility, prompt, alpha, and system color transitions match retail.
Telemetry ties each visible change to JDC script execution, UI tile writes, weapon/ammo queries, and the native spread state.

scenarios.title: Just Hit Marker
scenarios.trigger: Land a normal body hit, a headshot or critical hit, and a killing hit on deterministic actors.
assertions: The marker is caused by a real projectile or weapon hit and coincides with target health loss.
Hit classification, marker mode, color, scale, and fade match retail.
The hit event reaches JAM's registered handler and the resulting UI writes are recorded.

scenarios.title: Just Hit Indicator
scenarios.trigger: Receive deterministic hits from actors positioned in front, right, rear, and left quadrants.
assertions: Each hit removes player health and produces the matching screen-space direction.
Indicator rotation, alpha, duration, and fade match retail.
Telemetry records attacker position, player heading, computed angle, event dispatch, and UI write.

scenarios.title: Just Loot Menu
scenarios.trigger: Aim at the deterministic container, scroll its list, take one item, take a stack, equip or use an eligible item, and move the crosshair away.
assertions: The menu uses JAM's JLM XML and reflects the container's authoritative contents, counts, condition, and ownership.
Taking items mutates both the real container and player inventory exactly once.
Crosshair, inventory, key, scroll, and close-container event paths are recorded without opening a substitute proof menu.

scenarios.title: Just Visual Objectives
scenarios.trigger: Activate the deterministic quest objective, rotate and translate the camera, walk toward it, then complete or deactivate it.
assertions: The marker is bound to the real active objective target and uses JAM's JVO assets.
World-to-screen coordinates and displayed distance update while the camera and player move.
Objective query, coordinate callback, projection, and UI writes are recorded.

scenarios.title: Just Weapon Wheel
scenarios.trigger: Hold the configured wheel key, sweep across multiple populated slices, select a different weapon, release, reopen, and cancel.
assertions: The wheel uses JAM's JWH XML and DDS assets and is populated from the real inventory.
Mouse or stick angle selects the same slice as retail and the chosen weapon is actually equipped.
Key, menu, tab, inventory, UDF, and equip paths are recorded.

scenarios.title: Just Bullet Time
scenarios.trigger: Activate bullet time, walk, aim, fire and hit a target while active, hold until the configured resource decreases, then deactivate.
assertions: Simulation time changes through the native time system while input, animation, audio, projectiles, and UI obey the retail policy.
The configured resource drains from the authoritative actor value and normal time is restored exactly once.
Key, main-loop, hit, fire-weapon, coordinate, UDF, time, and actor-value paths are recorded.

scenarios.title: Just Hold Breath
scenarios.trigger: Aim through a supported weapon sight, measure idle sway, hold the configured key, keep aiming until the resource decreases, then release.
assertions: The observed weapon or camera sway falls while hold breath is active and returns after release.
Activation is rejected outside the valid aiming state and the configured resource changes only while active.
Key, aiming-state, spread or sway, actor-value, and UI paths are recorded.

scenarios.title: Just Vanilla Sprint
scenarios.trigger: From the save-relative heading minus 15 degrees, record a collision-free baseline run, sprint, turn while sprinting, jump if enabled, release, and recover.
assertions: Baseline and sprint speeds match the retail oracle within five percent and sprint ratio remains between 1.65 and 1.85.
Action Points drain during sprint and recover after release.
JAM's actual KF animation and WAV sound assets are observed by the native animation and audio systems.
Cloud displacement per real second and per simulation second matches retail within five percent, proving locomotion does not corrupt world time.

scenarios.title: JAM configuration and save/reload persistence
scenarios.trigger: Change one visible setting for every JAM module, save, quit to desktop, relaunch, load, verify all values and event registrations, then restore the fixture configuration.
assertions: Arrays, strings, globals, UDF references, registered events, INI values, and compatibility-owned serialized state round-trip according to retail semantics.
Every module remains functional after reload, demonstrated by one short post-load action per module.
No stale callback, duplicate event, double item transfer, double resource drain, or duplicate UI node appears.

scenarios.title: kNVSE provider attestation
scenarios.trigger: Run the labelled compatibility probe against a real JAM sprint KF asset: install override, play it, observe animation-controller state, remove override, and replay the original animation.
assertions: The overlay explicitly states that JAM 4.6 has zero active direct kNVSE calls.
A real kNVSE-compatible call reaches the native animation controller and visibly changes the played animation.
The override is removed cleanly and does not leak into subsequent JAM scenarios.
